Option 1: "جهد آن کن تا مگر نامت بماند جاودانی - جاودان کس را نشان باقی نخواهد ماند هرگز"
Translation: "Strive so that perhaps your name remains eternal - No eternal trace will ever remain for anyone"
This seems contradictory. The first line says "strive to make your name eternal" but the second line says "no eternal trace remains for anyone." This is about the futility of seeking eternal fame - it's a warning that nothing lasts forever, even names. The concept is about impermanence and the vanity of worldly ambition.

Option 2: "فردا غبار کالبدش در هوا رود - دامن کشان که می رود امروز بر زمین"
Translation: "Tomorrow his body's dust will fly in the air - Dragging his hem as he walks today on the ground"
This is about mortality. The person walking on earth today will become dust tomorrow. It's about the transience of life and death. The concept is impermanence and mortality.

Option 3: "وانکه دردیش نباشد به جهان هیچ کس است - هیچ کس نیست که او را به جهان دردی نیست"
Translation: "He who has no pain in the world is no one - There is no one in the world who has no pain"
This is about universal suffering. Everyone has pain/suffering. The concept is that suffering is universal and inevitable.

Translation: "Everything that is fitting and unfitting will go - They went and we will go, and whoever comes will go"
This is about impermanence - everything passes, everyone dies. The concept is universal transience and mortality.
